- Convert x to string s; handle negatives by storing sign and operating on the absolute value’s digits. Let n = len(s). If n == 0 or n == 1 or shift == 0, return s with sign applied.
- If shift > n, return reversed digits (s[::-1]) with original sign applied; else compute k = shift % n. Perform right circular shift by taking tail = s[-k:] + s[:-k].
- Return the resulting digit string with sign prefixed if x was negative (no stripping of leading zeros beyond what string operations naturally produce).
